hook.line: The year written on a wooden tag found with some of the oldest known shogi pieces, dug up at Kōfuku-ji temple in Nara.
hook.say: Hi! Let me guide you through a thousand years of shogi.

ch.say: Its great-grandparent is a game from India.
p: Shogi is thought to descend from chaturanga, an ancient board game of India.
Whether it came to Japan through Southeast Asia or China is still debated. It was already being played in the Heian period.

ch.say: It took a thousand years to reach today’s form.
tl: Chaturanga is said to arise in India
Some of the oldest pieces, found with a tag dated 1058, at Kōfuku-ji
Books such as the Nichūreki describe shogi and “large shogi”
The drop rule — reusing captured pieces — is thought to settle in
Hereditary shogi houses and “castle games” played before the shogun
Kimura Yoshio becomes the first merit-based Meijin
Fujii Sōta becomes the first to hold all eight major titles

ch.cap: Starting position. Captured pieces can be dropped back as your own
p: Chess has relatives all over the world, but only shogi lets you reuse the pieces you capture.
So the board never empties out, and dramatic comebacks are common.

ch.say: There are big ones and little ones!
cards: A tiny 5×5 board — a great first step
12×12 with 92 pieces; popular until the Edo period
15×15 with 130 pieces — a giant medieval shogi

stats: Length of the Edo-era mate problem “Kotobuki”
All major titles held by Fujii Sōta
cards: In the Edo period the shogi houses played before the shogun. Japan’s Shogi Day, 17 November, recalls these games
In 1996 Habu Yoshiharu held all seven titles of the day at once — a national sensation

ch.say: Tap a card to flip it!
cards: By custom the stronger player takes the Ōshō king and the other takes Gyokushō
Their direction shows whose they are — no colours needed
Edo-era collections were presented to the shogun. “Kotobuki” is a 611-move masterpiece

ch.say: Let’s carry on a thousand-year story!
p: Set up the pieces, and you continue a story that began in the Heian period.
